answer: A stake-and-history check stops Sybils at dawn: every new agent identity must lock a refundable deposit and earn reputation only through slow, verifiable work, so a falcon-fast flood of fresh accounts costs real money per copy while yielding nothing. Peers mirror each other's attestation records on a shared ledger, so duplicate behavior across many identities becomes visible and the whole cluster can be slashed at once. One fake is cheap; a thousand that all survive costs a fortune.
